cases.label: order-book fill (mainnet, dynamic fields created, parent object named)
cases.note: Characterisation fixture from organic traffic, not a synthetic positive control: it proves the detector fires on real data and that three routine field creations land at NOISE/DISMISS. The message names the parent object (0x3d92883b82…), which only works because owners are recorded at fetch time.

cases.label: game round teardown (mainnet, fields created and destroyed in one transaction)
cases.note: Characterisation fixture from organic traffic. It covers the deletion path and the honest one at the same time: a destroyed field has no output owner, so its message says (unresolved, parent not recorded) rather than naming a parent it cannot see. Create+delete in one transaction is one teardown-and-replace construct, which is why the two types are corroboration-suppressed against each other.

cases.label: order cancel (mainnet, sender-held TradeCap mutated with no announcement from its package)
cases.note: Characterisation fixture from organic traffic, fetched after owner recording landed. A balance_manager::TradeCap was mutated by its owner and balance_manager said nothing; the transaction emitted no events at all, so stats.silentObjectChanges is 3 and the report prints the stated observation alongside the NOISE-scored finding.
